clue.text: Smart deal

definitions.meaning: smart as an adjective means neat and well turned out
deal is the soft timber of a fir or pine, the same wood by another name

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as an adjective it means neat and trim, and as a noun it is a conifer whose timber is sold as deal.

clue.text: Quote to instal power units in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: to instal something is to set it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
amps, short for amperes, are units of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to quote a price for fitting electrical units in a temporary building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quote' looks like a price estimate, but it means to cite; 'instal' puts the power units inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A site for tents or caravans gives holidaymakers lodging that is not permanent.

clue.text: One not going straight will have to make this up

definitions.text: One not going straight will have to make this up

parts.words: One not going straight will have to make this up
parts.note: the surface suggests a criminal going straight, but it is a ship or aircraft blown off course by wind, which must recover the sideways drift

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not going straight' sounds like a crook, but it describes a vessel drifting downwind of its course.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is nautical for sideways drift caused by the wind, which a navigator must allow for and recover.

clue.text: His view of life is austere, one might say sour

definitions.text: His view of life is austere

indicators.note: signals that a word for sour is spoken, and the answer is the word it sounds like

parts.note: acetic means vinegary, sharp-tasting like acid

explanation.surface: A gloomy person's outlook is described as both severe and bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one might say' tells you a word for 'sour', ACETIC, is spoken; the answer sounds the same but is spelt with SC.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-denying person who rejects comfort and pleasure has a strict, severe outlook on living.

clue.text: Where T comes for pudding

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter T follows S, so the answer split in two describes where that letter sits

explanation.surface: A question about where tea fits into a meal, with pudding as the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T' looks like tea the drink, but it is the letter, which follows S in the alphabet; in Britain the dessert course has an informal name meaning what follows the main dish.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for dessert, the sweet course served following the main course.

clue.text: Rounded up but not rounded off

definitions.meaning: rounded up here means trapped or brought to bay, like cattle herded together
having angles rather than curved edges

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: trapped with no escape, and having sharp angles where edges meet rather than smooth curves.

clue.text: Drinking den provides address — no bother!

parts.note: to address an audience is to speak to it
something that is no bother is easy

explanation.surface: A bar offers a delivery address without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a street address but is the verb, to speak to.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit bar of the American Prohibition era is a classic example of a secret drinking den.

clue.text: Going out on a limb

definitions.meaning: walking out, on foot rather than riding
split as two words, the answer says on one foot, a foot being a limb

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: on the move by walking, and a phrase taken literally meaning standing on one leg or limb.

clue.text: Contents of magazine now purged, re-issued

indicators.note: something re-issued is put out again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine's contents have been cleaned up and published again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is an ammunition store; 're-issued' rearranges NOW PURGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is also a store for explosives and ammunition, and this explosive powder is what it holds.

clue.text: Seabirds wheeling around stern

indicators.note: birds wheeling around circle about, so the letters of the word are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Seabirds circle around the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' is the rear of a boat in the picture; 'wheeling around' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These are slender, fork-tailed seabirds related to gulls.

clue.text: Disorientated Indo-European god

indicators.note: someone disorientated is confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A confused deity from the Indo-European tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indo-European' reads as one word, but it splits: 'Disorientated' rearranges INDO, leaving 'European god' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology was worshipped in northern Europe.

clue.text: Attest to extremely absorbing Kipling poem

indicators.note: one piece absorbing another takes it in, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: extremely means very
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem of advice to a son

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for a very engrossing Kipling poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' looks like it describes the poem as gripping, but it is the container signal. The Kipling poem is the famous one of advice to a son.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest to a fact is to confirm or bear witness that it is true.

clue.text: Venture on the river for work

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows it here, so the venture comes second

parts.note: the Indus is a major river of Pakistan
to venture is to try

explanation.surface: An enterprise on a river looking for employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the venture after the river in an across answer; 'the river' is the long river of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard work and diligence are called this, as in a person noted for their application.

clue.text: Shattered hope and returning trouble robbed her of will to live

definitions.text: Shattered hope and returning trouble robbed her of will to live

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged
returning means going back, so the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A woman's broken hopes and troubles made her lose the wish to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' rearranges HOPE into OPHE; 'returning' turns AIL into LIA. The whole clue also describes Hamlet's tragic heroine, who drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, the heroine loses her reason and her will to go on after her father's death and the prince's rejection.

clue.text: A characteristic of houses, say

definitions.meaning: a distinctive quality or attribute of a substance
buildings and land owned are real estate, with houses an example

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an attribute of a thing, and real estate owned, of which houses are an example.

clue.text: Where barristers get refreshers?

parts.note: refreshers are both extra fees paid to barristers and drinks, and the London societies of barristers share their name with pubs

explanation.walkthrough: A refresher is a barrister's extra fee for a long case; barristers in London belong to one of four Inns of Court, and an inn is also a pub serving refreshing drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs serve refreshments, and the Inns of Court are the professional societies to which English barristers belong.

clue.text: "A person of importance?": murder detective's first question?

definitions.meaning: someone who is somebody, of any standing at all
split in two, the answer asks whether there is a corpse

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: someone of some significance, and read as two words, an inquiry whether there is a corpse.

clue.text: Underwear packed for one who's smart

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
something packed is placed in a box

explanation.surface: A piece of underwear has been packed for a clever person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed' gives IN BOX, as goods packed are put in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a very clever person, someone with lots of brains.

clue.text: A number, for example, press for some form of restraint

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Pressing a number of items, for example, as a kind of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to smooth clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shackle fastened round a prisoner's ankle is a means of restraining movement.

clue.text: French university in German city's resentful about it

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it, so the city goes inside

parts.note: to feel sore is to feel aggrieved or resentful
Bonn is a German city, the former West German capital

explanation.surface: Someone in a German city is resentful about a French university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the German city, the former West German capital, inside the word for resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic University of Paris is known by this name.

clue.text: Publican with no end of trade

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: a bartender serves drinks in a pub

explanation.surface: A pub landlord with endless commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like 'endless', but it takes the letters END out of BARTENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange goods without money is a form of trading.

clue.text: Meat in an iron container cooked in blazing brandy

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, here holding the meat
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: Meat in an iron pot cooked with flaming brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' gives FE, the chemical symbol, which holds LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Food doused in spirit and set alight is described with this French culinary term.

clue.text: One inside wards off evil spirits

indicators.note: one piece inside another sits within it

parts.note: to fend off an attack is to ward it off
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone within keeps away evil spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts I inside FENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Demons or devils are wicked spirits.

clue.text: Indisposed and laid up when advertised to appear

annotationWithheld.why: Indisposed and laid up when advertised to appear (6): ILL inside BED, but 'laid up' must give BED and also signal the container (in bed), one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Indisposed and laid up when advertised to appear

clue.text: Information about art form

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Facts about a kind of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A category or style of artistic work, such as the thriller in fiction.

clue.text: It provides the broad view of photography

definitions.text: It provides the broad view of photography

parts.words: It provides the broad view of photography
parts.note: a camera lens that takes in a larger field than normal

explanation.definitionFit: This type of camera lens has a short focal length and captures a wide field of vision.

clue.text: Sprinkle the last of the pepper in the hash

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a hash is a stew of chopped meat

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to sprinkle the remaining pepper into a hash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last of' takes R from pepper, and 'in' puts it inside STEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter something loosely over a surface is to sprinkle it.

clue.text: An admired sport

parts.note: sport here means a person who takes things well; this one is admired for gracious defeat

explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks like a game, but it means a good-natured person, here one who is gracious in defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts losing gracefully is respected as a decent sport.
